q: All of the following form the pelvic brim EXCEPT:
opts: Ischial tuberosities which lie at the pelvic outlet below the ischial spines
Sacral promontory and sacro-iliac joint margin of the ala of sacrum posteriorly
Iliopectineal line forming the lateral boundary of the pelvic brim
Upper border of ascending rami of pubic bone and pubic crest anteriorly

q: Fill up: The part of pelvis above the brim is ______ and its role in labour is ______.
opts: false pelvis; no role in labour – it supports the uterus
true pelvis; the whole of labour from engagement to expulsion
mid pelvis; internal rotation of the fetal head during labour
pelvic outlet; extension of the head during delivery

q: Which of the following statements about true pelvis parts is TRUE?
opts: True pelvis comprises inlet, cavity, mid-pelvis and outlet from above downwards
True pelvis comprises brim, ala, sacrum and coccyx as its four main parts
True pelvis comprises inlet, outlet, sacrum and symphysis as its four parts
True pelvis comprises cavity, brim, spines and tuberosities as its four parts

q: Match anteroposterior diameters of pelvic inlet — 1) True conjugate 2) Obstetric conjugate 3) Diagonal conjugate … A) 11 cm B) 10.5 cm C) 12 cm
Fill up: The smallest and most important conjugate of the pelvic inlet is ______.
opts: obstetric conjugate
true conjugate
diagonal conjugate
bituberous diameter

q: Fill up: Critical obstetric conjugate below which vaginal delivery is impossible is ______ cm; below ______ cm means contracted pelvis.
Which of the following statements about transverse diameter of inlet is TRUE?
opts: Transverse diameter is 13 cm between farthest points on iliopectineal line, greater than AP diameters
Transverse diameter is 11 cm same as true conjugate of pelvic inlet in gynaecoid pelvis
Transverse diameter is 12 cm which is oblique diameter from sacro-iliac joint
Transverse diameter is 10 cm which is transverse diameter of plane of least dimension

q: Which of the following statements about oblique diameters of inlet is TRUE?
opts: Oblique diameters 12 cm run from sacro-iliac joint to iliopectineal eminence on opposite side
Oblique diameters run from one ischial spine straight across to opposite ischial spine
Oblique diameters run from symphysis pubis directly backwards to sacral promontory
Oblique diameters run from one ischial tuberosity across to opposite tuberosity

q: Fill up: Contracted pelvis on clinical pelvimetry is flagged when obstetric conjugate is below ______ cm or diagonal conjugate below ______ cm.
Which of the following statements about pelvic cavity shape is TRUE?
opts: Pelvic cavity is truncated cylinder with shallow anterior wall and deep concave posterior wall
Pelvic cavity is true cylinder with anterior and posterior walls of equal depth throughout
Pelvic cavity is funnel shaped with deep anterior wall behind the pubic bone
Pelvic cavity is cuboid with flat posterior wall formed by sacrum and coccyx

q: Fill up: Posterior boundary of plane of greatest dimensions is ______ and of plane of least dimensions is ______.
opts: junction of S2–S3; junction of S4–S5
junction of S4–S5; junction of S2–S3
coccyx tip; coccyx tip
promontory; promontory

q: Fill up: Lateral extent of plane of greatest dimensions is ______ and of plane of least dimensions is ______.
opts: obturator foramen; ischial spines
ischial spines; obturator foramen
ischial tuberosities; spines
ala; tuberosities

q: Match pelvic plane with diameters — 1) Plane of greatest dimensions 2) Plane of least dimensions … A) 12.5–13 cm AP and 13 cm transverse B) 11.5 cm AP and 10 cm bispinous
Which of the following statements about bispinous diameter is TRUE?
opts: Bispinous diameter is smallest pelvic diameter and most important obstetrically at 10 cm
Bispinous diameter has no obstetric significance and is not measured clinically
Bispinous diameter is 13 cm wide at the plane of greatest dimensions
Bispinous diameter is measured at the obturator foramen in mid-pelvis

q: Fill up: Mid-pelvis is said to be contracted when interischial diameter is <______ cm.
